way-of-life.theme_name: Way of Life · Way of Death

rows.left: The fear of Adonai leads to life; one who has it is satisfied and rests untouched by evil.
rows.full: The fear of Adonai leads to life; one who has it is satisfied and rests untouched by evil.

rows.left: For the prudent, the path of life goes upward; thus he avoids Sh’ol below.
rows.full: For the prudent, the path of life goes upward; thus he avoids Sh’ol below.

rows.left: Good common sense produces grace, but the way of the treacherous is rough.
rows.full: Good common sense produces grace, but the way of the treacherous is rough.

rows.left: He who walks purely walks securely, but he who walks in crooked ways will be found out.
rows.full: He who walks purely walks securely, but he who walks in crooked ways will be found out.

rows.left: A person may plan his path, but Adonai directs his steps.
rows.full: A person may plan his path, but Adonai directs his steps.

rows.left: The fear of Adonai adds length to life, but the years of the wicked are cut short.
rows.full: The fear of Adonai adds length to life, but the years of the wicked are cut short.

rows.left: He who observes discipline is on the way to life; but he who ignores correction is making a mistake.
rows.full: He who observes discipline is on the way to life; but he who ignores correction is making a mistake.

rows.right: Whoever robs mother or father and says, “That’s not a crime!” is comrade to the destroyer.
rows.full: Whoever robs mother or father and says, “That’s not a crime!” is comrade to the destroyer.

rows.left: In the road of righteousness is life
rows.right: no death is in its pathway.
rows.full: In the road of righteousness is life; no death is in its pathway.

rows.right: A prostitute is a deep ditch, and a forbidden woman like a narrow well.
rows.full: A prostitute is a deep ditch, and a forbidden woman like a narrow well.

rows.left: No one is made secure by wickedness, but the roots of the righteous will never be moved.
rows.full: No one is made secure by wickedness, but the roots of the righteous will never be moved.

rows.left: What the righteous hope for will end in joy; what the wicked expect will come to nothing.
rows.full: What the righteous hope for will end in joy; what the wicked expect will come to nothing.

rows.left: The way of Adonai is a stronghold to the upright but ruin to those who do evil.
rows.full: The way of Adonai is a stronghold to the upright but ruin to those who do evil.

rows.left: The righteous will never be moved, but the wicked will not remain in the land.
rows.full: The righteous will never be moved, but the wicked will not remain in the land.

rows.left: To a fool, vileness is like a game, as is wisdom to a person of discernment.
rows.full: To a fool, vileness is like a game, as is wisdom to a person of discernment.

rows.left: What a fool dreads will overtake him, but the righteous will be given his desire.
rows.full: What a fool dreads will overtake him, but the righteous will be given his desire.

rows.left: When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone; but the righteous are firmly established forever.
rows.full: When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone; but the righteous are firmly established forever.

rows.left: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the duplicity of the treacherous destroys them.
rows.full: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the duplicity of the treacherous destroys them.

rows.left: A man who is kind does himself good, but the cruel does harm to himself.
rows.full: A man who is kind does himself good, but the cruel does harm to himself.

rows.left: The righteous desire only good, but what the wicked hope for brings wrath.
rows.full: The righteous desire only good, but what the wicked hope for brings wrath.

rows.left: He who strives for good obtains favor, but he who searches for evil — it comes to him!
rows.full: He who strives for good obtains favor, but he who searches for evil — it comes to him!

rows.left: Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil, but for those advising peace there is joy.
rows.full: Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil, but for those advising peace there is joy.

rows.left: No harm can come to the righteous, but the wicked are overwhelmed with disaster.
rows.full: No harm can come to the righteous, but the wicked are overwhelmed with disaster.

rows.left: The light of the righteous [shines] joyfully, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
rows.full: The light of the righteous [shines] joyfully, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

rows.left: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will suffer.
rows.full: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will suffer.

rows.left: There can be a way which seems right to a person, but at its end are the ways of death.
rows.full: There can be a way which seems right to a person, but at its end are the ways of death.

rows.left: One who doesn’t think believes every word, but the cautious understands his steps.
rows.full: One who doesn’t think believes every word, but the cautious understands his steps.

rows.left: Won’t those who plot evil go astray? But grace and truth are for those who plan good.
rows.full: Won’t those who plot evil go astray? But grace and truth are for those who plan good.

rows.left: Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.
rows.full: Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.

rows.left: Folly appeals to one who lacks sense, but a person of discernment goes straight ahead.
rows.full: Folly appeals to one who lacks sense, but a person of discernment goes straight ahead.

rows.left: Grace and truth atone for iniquity, and people turn from evil through fear of Adonai.
rows.full: Grace and truth atone for iniquity, and people turn from evil through fear of Adonai.

rows.left: Avoiding evil is the highway of the upright; he who watches his step preserves his life.
rows.full: Avoiding evil is the highway of the upright; he who watches his step preserves his life.

rows.left: There can be a way which seems right to a person, but at its end are the ways of death.
rows.full: There can be a way which seems right to a person, but at its end are the ways of death.

rows.left: One can cast lots into one’s lap, but the decision comes from Adonai.
rows.full: One can cast lots into one’s lap, but the decision comes from Adonai.

rows.left: A person’s own folly is what ruins his way, but he rages in his heart against Adonai.
rows.full: A person’s own folly is what ruins his way, but he rages in his heart against Adonai.

rows.left: He who keeps a mitzvah keeps himself safe, but he who doesn’t care how he lives will die.
rows.full: He who keeps a mitzvah keeps himself safe, but he who doesn’t care how he lives will die.

rows.left: One can devise many plans in one’s mind, but Adonai’s plan will prevail.
rows.full: One can devise many plans in one’s mind, but Adonai’s plan will prevail.

rows.left: Most people announce that they show kindness, but who can find someone faithful [enough to do it]?
rows.full: Most people announce that they show kindness, but who can find someone faithful [enough to do it]?

rows.left: A man’s steps are ordered by Adonai, so how can a person understand his own ways?
rows.full: A man’s steps are ordered by Adonai, so how can a person understand his own ways?

rows.left: A horse may be prepared for the day of battle, but victory comes from Adonai.
rows.full: A horse may be prepared for the day of battle, but victory comes from Adonai.

rows.left: You, my son: listen, be wise, and set your mind on the right way.
rows.full: You, my son: listen, be wise, and set your mind on the right way.

rows.right: She lies in wait to snatch her prey and adds to the number of faithless men.
rows.full: She lies in wait to snatch her prey and adds to the number of faithless men.

rows.left: He who conceals his sins will not succeed; he who confesses and abandons them will gain mercy.
rows.full: He who conceals his sins will not succeed; he who confesses and abandons them will gain mercy.

rows.left: Whoever lives blamelessly will be saved, but he whose ways are crooked will fall in one [of those ways].
rows.full: Whoever lives blamelessly will be saved, but he whose ways are crooked will fall in one [of those ways].

rows.left: Fearing human beings is a snare; but he who trusts in Adonai will be raised high [above danger].
rows.full: Fearing human beings is a snare; but he who trusts in Adonai will be raised high [above danger].

rows.right: A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
rows.full: A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

rows.left: The righteous live a life of integrity; happy are their children after them.
rows.full: The righteous live a life of integrity; happy are their children after them.

rows.right: The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.
rows.full: The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.

rows.right: For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.
rows.full: For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.

rows.left: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who is wise wins souls.
rows.full: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who is wise wins souls.

rows.left: The name of Adonai is a strong tower; a righteous person runs to it and is raised high [above danger].
rows.full: The name of Adonai is a strong tower; a righteous person runs to it and is raised high [above danger].

rows.left: Acting justly is a joy for the righteous
rows.right: it terrifies evildoers.
rows.full: Acting justly is a joy for the righteous but it terrifies evildoers.

rows.left: A wise man can go up into a city of warriors and undermine the strength in which it trusts.
rows.full: A wise man can go up into a city of warriors and undermine the strength in which it trusts.

rows.right: Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.
rows.full: Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.

rows.right: When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.
rows.full: When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.

rows.right: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.
rows.full: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.

rows.right: Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.
rows.full: Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.

rows.right: Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.
rows.full: Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.

rows.right: Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.
rows.full: Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.

rows.right: A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.
rows.full: A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.

rows.right: You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.
rows.full: You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.

rows.left: With his mouth the hypocrite can ruin his neighbor, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.
rows.full: With his mouth the hypocrite can ruin his neighbor, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.

rows.right: A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.
rows.full: A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.

rows.left: The righteousness of the upright rescues them, but the treacherous are trapped by their own intrigues.
rows.full: The righteousness of the upright rescues them, but the treacherous are trapped by their own intrigues.

rows.left: Don’t lurk like an outlaw near the home of the righteous, don’t raid the place where he lives.
rows.full: Don’t lurk like an outlaw near the home of the righteous, don’t raid the place where he lives.

rows.right: He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.
rows.full: He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.

rows.left: The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life, enabling one to avoid deadly traps.
rows.full: The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life, enabling one to avoid deadly traps.

rows.right: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.
rows.full: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.

rows.right: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;
rows.full: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;

rows.left: Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry
rows.right: he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
rows.full: Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.

rows.left: Blessings are for the head of the righteous
rows.right: the speech of the wicked is a cover for violence.
rows.full: Blessings are for the head of the righteous, but the speech of the wicked is a cover for violence.

rows.left: The memory of the righteous will be for a blessing
rows.right: the reputation of the wicked will rot.
rows.full: The memory of the righteous will be for a blessing, but the reputation of the wicked will rot.

rows.left: Wise-hearted people take orders
rows.right: a babbling fool will have trouble.
rows.full: Wise-hearted people take orders, but a babbling fool will have trouble.

rows.left: The righteous is delivered from trouble, and the wicked comes to take his place.
rows.full: The righteous is delivered from trouble, and the wicked comes to take his place.

rows.left: When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices
rows.right: and when the wicked perish, there is joy.
rows.full: When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices; and when the wicked perish, there is joy.

rows.left: A righteous man takes care of his animal
rows.right: the wicked? Even his compassion is cruel.
rows.full: A righteous man takes care of his animal, but the wicked? Even his compassion is cruel.

rows.left: A righteous person hates lying
rows.right: the wicked is vile and disgraceful.
rows.full: A righteous person hates lying, but the wicked is vile and disgraceful.

rows.left: Adonai detests the sacrifices of the wicked
rows.right: delights in the prayers of the upright.
rows.full: Adonai detests the sacrifices of the wicked but delights in the prayers of the upright.

rows.left: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
rows.full: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.

rows.left: In an evil person’s crime is a trap
rows.right: the righteous sing and rejoice.
rows.full: In an evil person’s crime is a trap, but the righteous sing and rejoice.

rows.left: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them
rows.right: but the house of the upright endures.
rows.full: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.

rows.left: The righteous person eats his fill
rows.right: the belly of the wicked is empty.
rows.full: The righteous person eats his fill, but the belly of the wicked is empty.

rows.right: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.
rows.full: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.

rows.right: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.
rows.full: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.

rows.left: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless
rows.right: likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.right: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.
rows.full: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.

rows.right: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!
rows.full: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!

rows.right: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.
rows.full: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.

rows.left: The wicked flee when no one pursues them
rows.right: but the righteous, like lions, feel sure of themselves.
rows.full: The wicked flee when no one pursues them; but the righteous, like lions, feel sure of themselves.

rows.left: When the wicked rise up, people hide
rows.right: but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
rows.full: When the wicked rise up, people hide; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.

rows.left: If the righteous are paid what they deserve here on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
rows.full: If the righteous are paid what they deserve here on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

rows.left: The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked
rows.right: he overthrows the wicked to their ruin.
rows.full: The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked; he overthrows the wicked to their ruin.

rows.left: By the blessing of the upright, a city is raised up
rows.right: but the words of the wicked tear it down.
rows.full: By the blessing of the upright, a city is raised up; but the words of the wicked tear it down.

rows.right: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
rows.full: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

rows.right: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.left: A wise person fears and turns away from evil
rows.right: a fool is reckless and overconfident.
rows.full: A wise person fears and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.

rows.right: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.
rows.full: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.

rows.left: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing
rows.right: the righteous can be confident even at death.
rows.full: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.

rows.right: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.
rows.full: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.

rows.left: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes
rows.right: but the righteous will witness their downfall.
rows.full: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.

rows.left: The plans of the righteous are just
rows.right: the schemes of the wicked are deceitful.
rows.full: The plans of the righteous are just, but the schemes of the wicked are deceitful.

rows.left: A backslider is filled up with his own ways, but a good person gets satisfaction from himself.
rows.full: A backslider is filled up with his own ways, but a good person gets satisfaction from himself.

rows.right: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;
rows.full: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;

rows.left: The righteous guides his friend’s way rightly
rows.right: the way of the wicked will lead them astray.
rows.full: The righteous guides his friend’s way rightly, but the way of the wicked will lead them astray.

rows.right: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.
rows.full: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.

rows.right: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.
rows.full: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.

rows.left: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father
rows.right: a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
rows.full: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.

rows.left: The heart’s real intentions are like deep water; but a person with discernment draws them out.
rows.full: The heart’s real intentions are like deep water; but a person with discernment draws them out.

rows.left: The wealth of the rich is his fortified city, like a high wall, in his own imagination.
rows.full: The wealth of the rich is his fortified city, like a high wall, in his own imagination.

rows.left: No good comes from ill-gotten wealth, but righteousness rescues from death.
rows.full: No good comes from ill-gotten wealth, but righteousness rescues from death.

rows.left: The righteousness of the innocent levels their way
rows.right: wickedness of the wicked makes them fall.
rows.full: The righteousness of the innocent levels their way, but wickedness of the wicked makes them fall.

rows.left: When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes; what he hopes for from evil comes to nothing.
rows.full: When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes; what he hopes for from evil comes to nothing.

rows.left: Righteousness protects him whose way is honest
rows.right: wickedness brings down the sinner.
rows.full: Righteousness protects him whose way is honest, but wickedness brings down the sinner.

rows.left: Adonai detests the way of the wicked
rows.right: loves anyone who pursues righteousness.
rows.full: Adonai detests the way of the wicked but loves anyone who pursues righteousness.

rows.left: When a man’s ways please Adonai, he makes even the man’s enemies be at peace with him.
rows.full: When a man’s ways please Adonai, he makes even the man’s enemies be at peace with him.

rows.left: The words of a man’s mouth are deep water, a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.
rows.full: The words of a man’s mouth are deep water, a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.

rows.left: He who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, prosperity and honor.
rows.full: He who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, prosperity and honor.

rows.left: The clever see trouble coming and hide; the simple go on and pay the penalty.
rows.full: The clever see trouble coming and hide; the simple go on and pay the penalty.

rows.left: The profits of the wicked are illusory
rows.right: but those who sow righteousness gain a true reward.
rows.full: The profits of the wicked are illusory; but those who sow righteousness gain a true reward.

rows.left: Genuine righteousness leads to life
rows.right: the pursuer of evil goes to his own death.
rows.full: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuer of evil goes to his own death.

rows.right: The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going, but the folly of fools misleads them.
rows.full: The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going, but the folly of fools misleads them.

rows.left: Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools
rows.right: but among the upright there is good will.
rows.full: Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools; but among the upright there is good will.

rows.right: Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.
rows.full: Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.

rows.right: One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.
rows.full: One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.

rows.right: He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.
rows.full: He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.

rows.right: The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.
rows.full: The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.

rows.right: Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.
rows.full: Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.

rows.right: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.
rows.full: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.

rows.right: for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.
rows.full: for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.

rows.left: For though he falls seven times, he will get up again; it’s the wicked who fail under stress.
rows.full: For though he falls seven times, he will get up again; it’s the wicked who fail under stress.

rows.right: Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.
rows.full: Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.

rows.left:
Better open rebuke than hidden love.

Wounds from a friend are received as well-meant, but an enemy’s kisses are insincere.
rows.full:
Better open rebuke than hidden love.

Wounds from a friend are received as well-meant, but an enemy’s kisses are insincere.

rows.left: The clever see trouble coming and hide; the thoughtless go on and pay the penalty.
rows.full: The clever see trouble coming and hide; the thoughtless go on and pay the penalty.

rows.left: When the just are triumphant, there is great rejoicing, but when the wicked rise up, people hide.
rows.full: When the just are triumphant, there is great rejoicing, but when the wicked rise up, people hide.

rows.right: Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.
rows.full: Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.

rows.left: the humble will be honored.
rows.right: The proud will be humbled
rows.full: The proud will be humbled, but the humble will be honored.

rows.left: but with the humble is wisdom.
rows.right: First comes pride, then disgrace
rows.full: First comes pride, then disgrace; but with the humble is wisdom.

rows.left: Better to be humble among the poor than share the spoil with the proud.
rows.right: Better to be humble among the poor than share the spoil with the proud.
rows.full: Better to be humble among the poor than share the spoil with the proud.

rows.left: before being honored, a person must be humble.
rows.right: Before being ruined, a person’s heart is proud
rows.full: Before being ruined, a person’s heart is proud; before being honored, a person must be humble.

rows.right: Haughty looks, a proud heart — what the wicked plow is sin.
rows.full: Haughty looks, a proud heart — what the wicked plow is sin.

rows.left: preserves intact the widow’s boundaries.
rows.right: Adonai will pull down the houses of the proud
rows.full: Adonai will pull down the houses of the proud, but preserves intact the widow’s boundaries.

rows.left: be assured that they will not go unpunished.
rows.right: Adonai detests all those with proud hearts
rows.full: Adonai detests all those with proud hearts; be assured that they will not go unpunished.

rows.right: Pride goes before destruction, and arrogance before failure.
rows.full: Pride goes before destruction, and arrogance before failure.

rows.left: Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what the day may bring.
rows.right: Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what the day may bring.
rows.full: Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what the day may bring.

rows.right: “Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.
rows.full: “Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.

rows.left: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.
rows.right: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.
rows.full: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.

rows.left: The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.
rows.full: The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.

rows.left: It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city
rows.right: their fights are like the bars of a fortress.
rows.full: It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city; their fights are like the bars of a fortress.

rows.left: A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense
rows.right: a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.
rows.full: A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense, but a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.

rows.left: A person with upright conduct fears Adonai
rows.right: a person who is devious scorns him.
rows.full: A person with upright conduct fears Adonai, but a person who is devious scorns him.

rows.left: All a man’s ways are pure in his own view
rows.right: Adonai weighs the spirit.
rows.full: All a man’s ways are pure in his own view, but Adonai weighs the spirit.

rows.left: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold
rows.right: the one who tests hearts is Adonai.
rows.full: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but the one who tests hearts is Adonai.

rows.left: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.
rows.right: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.
rows.full: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.

rows.left: All a person’s ways are right in his own view
rows.right: Adonai weighs the heart.
rows.full: All a person’s ways are right in his own view, but Adonai weighs the heart.

rows.left: The wicked is set on evil
rows.right: he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.
rows.full: The wicked is set on evil; he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.

rows.left: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.
rows.right: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.
rows.full: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.

rows.left: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.
rows.right: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.
rows.full: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.

rows.left: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.
rows.right: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.
rows.full: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.

rows.left: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold
rows.right: a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.
rows.full: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.

rows.left: Happy the person who is never without fear
rows.right: he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.
rows.full: Happy the person who is never without fear, but he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.

rows.left: The diligent will rule, while the lazy will be put to forced labor.
rows.right: The diligent will rule, while the lazy will be put to forced labor.
rows.full: The diligent will rule, while the lazy will be put to forced labor.

rows.left: so at harvest-time, when he looks, there is nothing.
rows.right: A lazy person won’t plow in winter
rows.full: A lazy person won’t plow in winter; so at harvest-time, when he looks, there is nothing.

rows.left: doesn’t have; the diligent get their desires filled.
rows.right: The lazy person wants
rows.full: The lazy person wants but doesn’t have; the diligent get their desires filled.

rows.left: but a righteous person gives without holding back.
rows.right: A lazy man’s craving will kill him, because his hands refuse to work — he covets greedily all day long
rows.full: A lazy man’s craving will kill him, because his hands refuse to work — he covets greedily all day long; but a righteous person gives without holding back.

rows.left: but when a man is diligent, his wealth is precious.
rows.right: A lazy man doesn’t roast what he hunted
rows.full: A lazy man doesn’t roast what he hunted; but when a man is diligent, his wealth is precious.

rows.left: diligent hands bring wealth.
rows.right: Idle hands bring poverty
rows.full: Idle hands bring poverty; diligent hands bring wealth.

rows.left: Whoever is lazy in doing his work is brother to the destroyer.
rows.right: Whoever is lazy in doing his work is brother to the destroyer.
rows.full: Whoever is lazy in doing his work is brother to the destroyer.

rows.right: Laziness makes people fall asleep, and an idle person will go hungry.
rows.full: Laziness makes people fall asleep, and an idle person will go hungry.

rows.left: The plans of the diligent lead only to abundance
rows.right: but all who rush in arrive only at want.
rows.full: The plans of the diligent lead only to abundance; but all who rush in arrive only at want.

rows.right: A lazy man says, “There’s a lion outside! I’ll be killed if I go out in the street!”
rows.full: A lazy man says, “There’s a lion outside! I’ll be killed if I go out in the street!”

rows.left: Do you see a man skilled at his work? He will serve kings, not obscure people.
rows.full: Do you see a man skilled at his work? He will serve kings, not obscure people.

rows.right: I passed by the field of the lazy man and the vineyard of the man lacking sense.
rows.full: I passed by the field of the lazy man and the vineyard of the man lacking sense.

rows.right: The lazy person says, “There’s a lion in the streets! A lion is roaming loose out there!” The door turns on its hinges, and the lazy man on his bed.
rows.full: The lazy person says, “There’s a lion in the streets! A lion is roaming loose out there!” The door turns on its hinges, and the lazy man on his bed.

rows.left: A sensible person gathers in summer
rows.right: he who sleeps during harvest is an embarrassment.
rows.full: A sensible person gathers in summer, but he who sleeps during harvest is an embarrassment.

rows.left: He who farms his land will have plenty of food
rows.right: he who follows futilities has no sense.
rows.full: He who farms his land will have plenty of food, but he who follows futilities has no sense.

rows.left: doesn’t even bother to bring it to his mouth.
rows.right: The lazy person buries his hand in the dish
rows.full: The lazy person buries his hand in the dish but doesn’t even bother to bring it to his mouth.

rows.left: is too tired to return it to his mouth.
rows.right: The lazy person buries his hand in the dish
rows.full: The lazy person buries his hand in the dish but is too tired to return it to his mouth.

rows.left: Prepare your outside work, and get things ready for yourself on the land
rows.right: after that, build your house.
rows.full: Prepare your outside work, and get things ready for yourself on the land; after that, build your house.

rows.right: Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes is a lazy person to his employer.
rows.full: Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes is a lazy person to his employer.

rows.right: A lazy man is wiser in his own view than seven who can answer with sense.
rows.full: A lazy man is wiser in his own view than seven who can answer with sense.

rows.left: the path of the upright is a level highway.
rows.right: The lazy person’s way seems overgrown by thorns
rows.full: The lazy person’s way seems overgrown by thorns, but the path of the upright is a level highway.

rows.left: He who farms his land will have plenty of food
rows.right: he who follows futilities will have plenty of poverty.
rows.full: He who farms his land will have plenty of food, but he who follows futilities will have plenty of poverty.

rows.left: In all work there is profit
rows.right: mere talk produces only poverty.
rows.full: In all work there is profit, but mere talk produces only poverty.

rows.left: the work of the pure is right.
rows.right: A criminal’s conduct is crooked
rows.full: A criminal’s conduct is crooked, but the work of the pure is right.

rows.left: He who has skill in a matter will succeed
rows.right: he who trusts in Adonai will be happy.
rows.full: He who has skill in a matter will succeed; he who trusts in Adonai will be happy.

rows.left: Where there are no oxen, the stalls are clean
rows.right: but much is produced by the strength of an ox.
rows.full: Where there are no oxen, the stalls are clean; but much is produced by the strength of an ox.

rows.right: “I’ll just lie here a bit, rest a little longer, just fold my hands for a little more sleep” — and poverty comes marching in on you, scarcity hits you like an invading soldier.
rows.full: “I’ll just lie here a bit, rest a little longer, just fold my hands for a little more sleep” — and poverty comes marching in on you, scarcity hits you like an invading soldier.

rows.left: The activity of the righteous is for life
rows.right: the income of the wicked is for sin.
rows.full: The activity of the righteous is for life; the income of the wicked is for sin.

rows.left: The crown of the wise is their riches
rows.right: the folly of fools is just that — folly.
rows.full: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools is just that — folly.

rows.left: keep your eyes open, and you’ll have plenty of food.
rows.right: If you love sleep, you will become poor
rows.full: If you love sleep, you will become poor; keep your eyes open, and you’ll have plenty of food.

rows.left: Food obtained by fraud may taste good
rows.right: later the mouth is full of gravel.
rows.full: Food obtained by fraud may taste good, but later the mouth is full of gravel.

rows.left: No good comes from ill-gotten wealth
rows.right: righteousness rescues from death.
rows.full: No good comes from ill-gotten wealth, but righteousness rescues from death.

rows.left: Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry
rows.right: he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
rows.full: Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.

rows.left: He who guarantees a loan for a stranger will suffer
rows.right: refusing to underwrite is safe.
rows.full: He who guarantees a loan for a stranger will suffer, but refusing to underwrite is safe.

rows.left: A working man’s appetite acts on his behalf, because his hunger presses him on.
rows.full: A working man’s appetite acts on his behalf, because his hunger presses him on.

rows.left: “Really bad stuff!” says the buyer [to the seller]
rows.right: then he goes off and brags [about his bargain].
rows.full: “Really bad stuff!” says the buyer [to the seller]; then he goes off and brags [about his bargain].

rows.left: Possessions acquired quickly at first will not be blessed in the end.
rows.right: Possessions acquired quickly at first will not be blessed in the end.
rows.full: Possessions acquired quickly at first will not be blessed in the end.

rows.left: the ground was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
rows.right: There it was, overgrown with thistles
rows.full: There it was, overgrown with thistles; the ground was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.

rows.left: I looked, and I thought about it
rows.right: I saw, and I learned this lesson:
rows.full: I looked, and I thought about it; I saw, and I learned this lesson:

rows.left: Whoever tends the fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who is attentive to his master will be honored.
rows.full: Whoever tends the fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who is attentive to his master will be honored.

rows.left:
Take care to know the condition of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds.

For wealth doesn’t last forever, neither does a crown through all generations.

When the hay has been mown, and the new grass appears, and the mountain greens have been gathered
rows.right:
the lambs will provide your clothing, the goats will sell for enough to buy a field,

and there will be enough goat’s milk to [buy] food for you and your household and maintenance for your servant-girls.
rows.full:
Take care to know the condition of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds.

For wealth doesn’t last forever, neither does a crown through all generations.

When the hay has been mown, and the new grass appears, and the mountain greens have been gathered;

the lambs will provide your clothing, the goats will sell for enough to buy a field,

and there will be enough goat’s milk to [buy] food for you and your household and maintenance for your servant-girls.

rows.left: People with good sense are slow to anger, and it is their glory to overlook an offense.
rows.full: People with good sense are slow to anger, and it is their glory to overlook an offense.

rows.left: hot-tempered people commit many crimes.
rows.right: Angry people stir up strife
rows.full: Angry people stir up strife; hot-tempered people commit many crimes.

rows.left: patient people quiet quarrels.
rows.right: Hot-tempered people stir up strife
rows.full: Hot-tempered people stir up strife, but patient people quiet quarrels.

rows.left: Being slow to anger goes with great understanding, being quick-tempered makes folly still worse.
rows.right: Being slow to anger goes with great understanding, being quick-tempered makes folly still worse.
rows.full: Being slow to anger goes with great understanding, being quick-tempered makes folly still worse.

rows.left: for any fool can explode in anger.
rows.right: Avoiding quarrels brings a person honor
rows.full: Avoiding quarrels brings a person honor; for any fool can explode in anger.

rows.left: who can stand up to jealousy?
rows.right: Fury is cruel and anger overwhelming
rows.full: Fury is cruel and anger overwhelming, but who can stand up to jealousy?

rows.left: Don’t associate with an angry man
rows.right: make no hot-tempered man your companion.
rows.full: Don’t associate with an angry man; make no hot-tempered man your companion.

rows.left: If there’s no wood, the fire goes out
rows.right:
if nobody gossips, contention stops.

As coals are to embers and wood to fire is a quarrelsome person to kindling strife.
rows.full:
If there’s no wood, the fire goes out; if nobody gossips, contention stops.

As coals are to embers and wood to fire is a quarrelsome person to kindling strife.

rows.right: A secret gift allays anger, and a bribe under the cloak the strongest fury.
rows.full: A secret gift allays anger, and a bribe under the cloak the strongest fury.

rows.left: He who is quick-tempered does stupid things, and one who does vile things is hated.
rows.right: He who is quick-tempered does stupid things, and one who does vile things is hated.
rows.full: He who is quick-tempered does stupid things, and one who does vile things is hated.

rows.left: Like someone who grabs a dog by the ears is a passer-by who mixes in a fight not his own.
rows.right: Like someone who grabs a dog by the ears is a passer-by who mixes in a fight not his own.
rows.full: Like someone who grabs a dog by the ears is a passer-by who mixes in a fight not his own.

rows.left: those who make their gates tall are courting disaster.
rows.right: Those who love quarreling love giving offense
rows.full: Those who love quarreling love giving offense; those who make their gates tall are courting disaster.

rows.left: A violent-tempered person will be punished
rows.right: if you try to save him from it, you make things worse.
rows.full: A violent-tempered person will be punished; if you try to save him from it, you make things worse.

rows.left: Hate stirs up disputes
rows.right: love covers all kinds of transgressions.
rows.full: Hate stirs up disputes, but love covers all kinds of transgressions.

rows.left: A tranquil mind gives health to the body
rows.right: envy rots the bones.
rows.full: A tranquil mind gives health to the body, but envy rots the bones.

rows.left: He who conceals an offense promotes love
rows.right: he who harps on it can separate even close friends.
rows.full: He who conceals an offense promotes love, but he who harps on it can separate even close friends.

rows.left: If you do, you may learn his ways and find yourself caught in a trap.
rows.right: If you do, you may learn his ways and find yourself caught in a trap.
rows.full: If you do, you may learn his ways and find yourself caught in a trap.

rows.left: With patience a ruler may be won over, and a gentle tongue can break bones.
rows.right: With patience a ruler may be won over, and a gentle tongue can break bones.
rows.full: With patience a ruler may be won over, and a gentle tongue can break bones.

rows.left: the wise can calm the fury.
rows.right: Scoffers can inflame a city
rows.full: Scoffers can inflame a city, but the wise can calm the fury.

rows.left:
2 Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth,
    a stranger and not your own lips.
rows.full:
2 Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth,
    a stranger and not your own lips.

rows.left:
23 Whoever guards his mouth and tongue
keeps himself out of trouble.
rows.full:
23 Whoever guards his mouth and tongue
keeps himself out of trouble.

rows.right:
27 A worthless person digs up evil [gossip] —
it is like scorching fire on his lips.
rows.full:
27 A worthless person digs up evil [gossip] —
it is like scorching fire on his lips.

rows.left:
18 He who covers up hate has lips that lie,
 and anyone who slanders is a fool.
19 When words are many, sin is not lacking
rows.right: so he who controls his speech is wise.
rows.full:
18 He who covers up hate has lips that lie,
 and anyone who slanders is a fool.
19 When words are many, sin is not lacking;
    so he who controls his speech is wise.

rows.left:
4 The words of a man’s mouth are deep water,
    a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.
rows.full:
4 The words of a man’s mouth are deep water,
    a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.

rows.left:
20 The tongue of the righteous is like pure silver,
 but the mind of the wicked is worth little.
21 The lips of the righteous feed many,
    but fools die for lack of sense.
rows.full:
20 The tongue of the righteous is like pure silver,
 but the mind of the wicked is worth little.
21 The lips of the righteous feed many,
    but fools die for lack of sense.

rows.left:
3 From the mouth of a fool sprouts pride,
but the lips of the wise protect them.
rows.full:
3 From the mouth of a fool sprouts pride,
but the lips of the wise protect them.

rows.left:
23 The wise man’s heart teaches his mouth,
 and to his lips it adds learning.
24 Pleasant words are like a honeycomb,
    sweet to the taste and healing for the body.
rows.full:
23 The wise man’s heart teaches his mouth,
 and to his lips it adds learning.
24 Pleasant words are like a honeycomb,
    sweet to the taste and healing for the body.

rows.right:
1 Don’t be envious of evil people,
 and don’t desire to be with them.
2 For their minds are occupied with violence,
    and their lips speak of making trouble.
rows.full:
1 Don’t be envious of evil people,
 and don’t desire to be with them.
2 For their minds are occupied with violence,
    and their lips speak of making trouble.

rows.left: 3 Set a guard, Adonai, over my mouth
rows.right:
keep watch at the door of my lips.
4 Don’t let my heart turn to anything evil
 or allow me to act wickedly
 with men who are evildoers;
 keep me from eating their delicacies.

rows.left:
31 The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom,
 but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
32 The lips of the righteous know what is wanted,
    but the mouth of the wicked [knows] deceit.
rows.full:
31 The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom,
 but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
32 The lips of the righteous know what is wanted,
    but the mouth of the wicked [knows] deceit.

rows.left:
12 The words spoken by the wise bring them favor,
 but the lips of a fool swallow him up.
13 What he says starts with foolishness
 and ends with wicked madness.
14 A fool keeps talking and talking,
 yet no one knows what the future will bring —
 can anyone tell a person
 what will happen after he’s gone?
15 The efforts of a fool wear him out;
 he doesn’t even know the way to town!
rows.full:
12 The words spoken by the wise bring them favor,
 but the lips of a fool swallow him up.
13 What he says starts with foolishness
 and ends with wicked madness.
14 A fool keeps talking and talking,
 yet no one knows what the future will bring —
 can anyone tell a person
 what will happen after he’s gone?
15 The efforts of a fool wear him out;
 he doesn’t even know the way to town!

rows.left:
7 Fine speech is unbecoming to a boor,
and even less lying lips to a leader.
rows.full:
7 Fine speech is unbecoming to a boor,
and even less lying lips to a leader.

rows.left: 13 On the lips of the intelligent is found wisdom
rows.right:
a stick is in store for the back of a fool.
14 Wise people hide their knowledge,
    but when a fool speaks, ruin is imminent.
rows.full:
13 On the lips of the intelligent is found wisdom,
 but a stick is in store for the back of a fool.
14 Wise people hide their knowledge,
    but when a fool speaks, ruin is imminent.

rows.left: Therefore my dear brothers, let every person be quick to listen but slow to speak, slow to get angry
rows.full: Therefore my dear brothers, let every person be quick to listen but slow to speak, slow to get angry

rows.left: 4 An evildoer heeds wicked lips
rows.right: a liar listens to destructive talk.
rows.full:
4 An evildoer heeds wicked lips;
a liar listens to destructive talk.

rows.left:
A wise man speaking quietly is more worth heeding
 than the shouts of a ruler commanding fools.
rows.full:
A wise man speaking quietly is more worth heeding
 than the shouts of a ruler commanding fools.

rows.left:
27 A knowledgeable person controls his tongue;
    a discerning person controls his temper.
rows.full:
27 A knowledgeable person controls his tongue;
    a discerning person controls his temper.

rows.left:
21 The lips of the righteous feed many,
but fools die for lack of sense.
rows.full:
21 The lips of the righteous feed many,
but fools die for lack of sense.

rows.left:
15 With patience a ruler may be won over,
and a gentle tongue can break bones.
rows.full:
15 With patience a ruler may be won over,
and a gentle tongue can break bones.

rows.left:
20 Do you see someone too anxious to speak?
There is more hope for a fool than for him.
rows.full:
20 Do you see someone too anxious to speak?
There is more hope for a fool than for him.

rows.right:
Don’t be a witness against your neighbor for no reason —
would you use your lips to deceive?
rows.full:
Don’t be a witness against your neighbor for no reason —
would you use your lips to deceive?

rows.left: 22 Lying lips are an abomination to Adonai
rows.right:
those who deal faithfully are his delight.
23 A cautious person conceals knowledge,
    but the heart of a fool blurts out folly.
rows.full:
22 Lying lips are an abomination to Adonai,
 but those who deal faithfully are his delight.
23 A cautious person conceals knowledge,
    but the heart of a fool blurts out folly.

rows.left:
7 The lips of the wise spread knowledge;
not so the hearts of fools.
rows.full:
7 The lips of the wise spread knowledge;
not so the hearts of fools.

rows.left:
15 A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls,
 but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.
rows.full:
15 A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls,
 but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.

rows.left:
13:14 The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life,
    enabling one to avoid deadly traps.
rows.full:
13:14 The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life,
    enabling one to avoid deadly traps.

rows.left:
11 A fool gives vent to all his feelings,
but the wise, thinking of afterwards, stills them.
rows.full:
11 A fool gives vent to all his feelings,
but the wise, thinking of afterwards, stills them.

rows.left:
10 He who winks his eye [instead of rebuking] causes pain,
yet a babbling fool will have trouble.
rows.full:
10 He who winks his eye [instead of rebuking] causes pain,
yet a babbling fool will have trouble.

rows.left:
30 The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, 
and he who is wise wins souls
rows.full:
30 The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, 
and he who is wise wins souls

rows.left:
11 He who loves the pure-hearted and is gracious in speech
will have the king as his friend.
rows.full:
11 He who loves the pure-hearted and is gracious in speech
will have the king as his friend.

rows.left:
9 When a wise man argues with a foolish one,
he meets anger and ridicule without relief.
rows.full:
9 When a wise man argues with a foolish one,
he meets anger and ridicule without relief.

rows.left: It is not good to be partial to the guilty and thus deprive the innocent of justice.
rows.full: It is not good to be partial to the guilty and thus deprive the innocent of justice.

rows.left: False scales are an abomination to Adonai, but accurate weights please him.
rows.full: False scales are an abomination to Adonai, but accurate weights please him.

rows.left: Adonai detests a double standard in weights, and false scales are not good.
rows.full: Adonai detests a double standard in weights, and false scales are not good.

rows.left: He who tells the truth furthers justice, but a false witness furthers deceit.
rows.full: He who tells the truth furthers justice, but a false witness furthers deceit.

rows.right: A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
rows.full: A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

rows.left: The righteous live a life of integrity; happy are their children after them.
rows.full: The righteous live a life of integrity; happy are their children after them.

rows.right: The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.
rows.full: The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.

rows.right: For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.
rows.full: For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.

rows.left: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who is wise wins souls.
rows.full: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who is wise wins souls.

rows.left: The name of Adonai is a strong tower; a righteous person runs to it and is raised high [above danger].
rows.full: The name of Adonai is a strong tower; a righteous person runs to it and is raised high [above danger].

rows.left: To do what is right and just is more pleasing to Adonai than sacrifice.
rows.full: To do what is right and just is more pleasing to Adonai than sacrifice.

rows.left: From under a cloak a bad man takes a bribe to pervert the course of justice.
rows.full: From under a cloak a bad man takes a bribe to pervert the course of justice.

rows.left: Acting justly is a joy for the righteous but it terrifies evildoers.
rows.full: Acting justly is a joy for the righteous but it terrifies evildoers.

rows.left: A wise man can go up into a city of warriors and undermine the strength in which it trusts.
rows.full: A wise man can go up into a city of warriors and undermine the strength in which it trusts.

rows.right: Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.
rows.full: Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.

rows.right: When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.
rows.full: When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.

rows.left: False weights and false measures — Adonai detests them both.
rows.full: False weights and false measures — Adonai detests them both.

rows.right: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.
rows.full: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.

rows.right: Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.
rows.full: Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.

rows.right: Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.
rows.full: Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.

rows.right: Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.
rows.full: Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.

rows.right: A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.
rows.full: A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.

rows.right: You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.
rows.full: You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.

rows.left: To show partiality is not good, though a person may do wrong for a crust of bread.
rows.full: To show partiality is not good, though a person may do wrong for a crust of bread.

rows.left: The fear of Adonai leads to life; one who has it is satisfied and rests untouched by evil.
rows.full: The fear of Adonai leads to life; one who has it is satisfied and rests untouched by evil.

rows.left: A worthless witness mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows wrongdoing.
rows.full: A worthless witness mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows wrongdoing.

rows.left: With his mouth the hypocrite can ruin his neighbor, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.
rows.full: With his mouth the hypocrite can ruin his neighbor, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.

rows.right: A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.
rows.full: A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.

rows.left: The righteousness of the upright rescues them, but the treacherous are trapped by their own intrigues.
rows.full: The righteousness of the upright rescues them, but the treacherous are trapped by their own intrigues.

rows.left: A false witness will not go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will not escape.
rows.full: A false witness will not go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will not escape.

rows.left: For the prudent, the path of life goes upward; thus he avoids Sh’ol below.
rows.full: For the prudent, the path of life goes upward; thus he avoids Sh’ol below.

rows.left: Don’t lurk like an outlaw near the home of the righteous, don’t raid the place where he lives.
rows.full: Don’t lurk like an outlaw near the home of the righteous, don’t raid the place where he lives.

rows.left: Good common sense produces grace, but the way of the treacherous is rough.
rows.full: Good common sense produces grace, but the way of the treacherous is rough.

rows.left: A truthful witness saves lives, but a liar misdirects [judgment].
rows.full: A truthful witness saves lives, but a liar misdirects [judgment].

rows.left: A false witness will not go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will perish.
rows.full: A false witness will not go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will perish.

rows.right: He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.
rows.full: He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.

rows.left: but with those who condemn him, things will go well, and a good blessing will come upon them.
rows.full: but with those who condemn him, things will go well, and a good blessing will come upon them.

rows.left: The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life, enabling one to avoid deadly traps.
rows.full: The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life, enabling one to avoid deadly traps.

rows.right: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.
rows.full: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.

rows.right: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;
rows.full: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;

rows.left: Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry
rows.right: he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
rows.full: Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.

rows.left: Blessings are for the head of the righteous
rows.right: the speech of the wicked is a cover for violence.
rows.full: Blessings are for the head of the righteous, but the speech of the wicked is a cover for violence.

rows.left: The memory of the righteous will be for a blessing
rows.right: the reputation of the wicked will rot.
rows.full: The memory of the righteous will be for a blessing, but the reputation of the wicked will rot.

rows.left: Wise-hearted people take orders, but a babbling fool will have trouble.
rows.full: Wise-hearted people take orders, but a babbling fool will have trouble.

rows.left: The righteous is delivered from trouble, and the wicked comes to take his place.
rows.full: The righteous is delivered from trouble, and the wicked comes to take his place.

rows.left: When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices
rows.right: and when the wicked perish, there is joy.
rows.full: When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices; and when the wicked perish, there is joy.

rows.left: A righteous man takes care of his animal
rows.right: the wicked? Even his compassion is cruel.
rows.full: A righteous man takes care of his animal, but the wicked? Even his compassion is cruel.

rows.left: A righteous person hates lying
rows.right: the wicked is vile and disgraceful.
rows.full: A righteous person hates lying, but the wicked is vile and disgraceful.

rows.left: Adonai detests the sacrifices of the wicked but delights in the prayers of the upright.
rows.full: Adonai detests the sacrifices of the wicked but delights in the prayers of the upright.

rows.left: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
rows.full: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.

rows.left: Evil people don’t understand justice, but those who seek Adonai understand everything.
rows.full: Evil people don’t understand justice, but those who seek Adonai understand everything.

rows.left: In an evil person’s crime is a trap, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
rows.full: In an evil person’s crime is a trap, but the righteous sing and rejoice.

rows.right: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.
rows.full: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.

rows.left: The righteous person eats his fill
rows.right: the belly of the wicked is empty.
rows.full: The righteous person eats his fill, but the belly of the wicked is empty.

rows.right: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.
rows.full: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.

rows.right: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.
rows.full: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.

rows.left: These also are sayings of the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
rows.full: These also are sayings of the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.

rows.right: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.right: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.
rows.full: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.

rows.right: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!
rows.full: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!

rows.right: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.
rows.full: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.

rows.left: The wicked flee when no one pursues them
rows.right: but the righteous, like lions, feel sure of themselves.
rows.full: The wicked flee when no one pursues them; but the righteous, like lions, feel sure of themselves.

rows.left: When the wicked rise up, people hide
rows.right: but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
rows.full: When the wicked rise up, people hide; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.

rows.left: If the righteous are paid what they deserve here on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
rows.full: If the righteous are paid what they deserve here on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

rows.left: The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked
rows.right: he overthrows the wicked to their ruin.
rows.full: The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked; he overthrows the wicked to their ruin.

rows.left: By the blessing of the upright, a city is raised up; but the words of the wicked tear it down.
rows.full: By the blessing of the upright, a city is raised up; but the words of the wicked tear it down.

rows.right: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
rows.full: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

rows.right: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.left: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but it is from Adonai that each gets justice.
rows.full: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but it is from Adonai that each gets justice.

rows.left: A wise person fears and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
rows.full: A wise person fears and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.

rows.right: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.
rows.full: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.

rows.left: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing
rows.right: the righteous can be confident even at death.
rows.full: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.

rows.right: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.
rows.full: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.

rows.left: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes
rows.right: but the righteous will witness their downfall.
rows.full: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.

rows.left: The plans of the righteous are just
rows.right: the schemes of the wicked are deceitful.
rows.full: The plans of the righteous are just, but the schemes of the wicked are deceitful.

rows.left: He who walks purely walks securely, but he who walks in crooked ways will be found out.
rows.full: He who walks purely walks securely, but he who walks in crooked ways will be found out.

rows.left: A backslider is filled up with his own ways, but a good person gets satisfaction from himself.
rows.full: A backslider is filled up with his own ways, but a good person gets satisfaction from himself.

rows.left: A person may plan his path, but Adonai directs his steps.
rows.full: A person may plan his path, but Adonai directs his steps.

rows.left: The first to state his case seems right, till the other one comes and cross-examines.
rows.full: The first to state his case seems right, till the other one comes and cross-examines.

rows.right: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;
rows.full: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;

rows.left: He who tells the guilty, “You are innocent,” will be cursed by peoples, reviled by nations;
rows.full: He who tells the guilty, “You are innocent,” will be cursed by peoples, reviled by nations;

rows.left: The righteous guides his friend’s way rightly
rows.right: the way of the wicked will lead them astray.
rows.full: The righteous guides his friend’s way rightly, but the way of the wicked will lead them astray.

rows.right: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.
rows.full: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.

rows.left: A lying witness is doomed, but one who heard [what was said] will testify successfully.
rows.full: A lying witness is doomed, but one who heard [what was said] will testify successfully.

rows.right: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.
rows.full: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.

rows.left: To punish the innocent is not right, likewise to flog noble people for their uprightness.
rows.full: To punish the innocent is not right, likewise to flog noble people for their uprightness.

rows.left: The fear of Adonai adds length to life
rows.right: the years of the wicked are cut short.
rows.full: The fear of Adonai adds length to life, but the years of the wicked are cut short.

rows.left: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
rows.full: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.

rows.left: The heart’s real intentions are like deep water; but a person with discernment draws them out.
rows.full: The heart’s real intentions are like deep water; but a person with discernment draws them out.

rows.left: Don’t exploit the helpless, because they are helpless, and don’t crush the poor in court,
rows.full: Don’t exploit the helpless, because they are helpless, and don’t crush the poor in court,

rows.left: He who justifies the wicked and he who condemns the righteous — both alike are an abomination to Adonai.
rows.full: He who justifies the wicked and he who condemns the righteous — both alike are an abomination to Adonai.

rows.left: The greedy for gain brings trouble to his home, but he who hates bribes will live.
rows.full: The greedy for gain brings trouble to his home, but he who hates bribes will live.

rows.left: He who observes discipline is on the way to life; but he who ignores correction is making a mistake.
rows.full: He who observes discipline is on the way to life; but he who ignores correction is making a mistake.

rows.right: Whoever robs mother or father and says, “That’s not a crime!” is comrade to the destroyer.
rows.full: Whoever robs mother or father and says, “That’s not a crime!” is comrade to the destroyer.

rows.left: In the road of righteousness is life
rows.right: no death is in its pathway.
rows.full: In the road of righteousness is life; no death is in its pathway.

rows.right: A prostitute is a deep ditch, and a forbidden woman like a narrow well.
rows.full: A prostitute is a deep ditch, and a forbidden woman like a narrow well.

rows.left: No one is made secure by wickedness
rows.right: the roots of the righteous will never be moved.
rows.full: No one is made secure by wickedness, but the roots of the righteous will never be moved.

rows.left: The oppressor of the poor insults his maker
rows.right: he who is kind to the needy honors him.
rows.full: The oppressor of the poor insults his maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.

rows.left: A poor man who oppresses the weak is like a downpour that sweeps away all the food.
rows.full: A poor man who oppresses the weak is like a downpour that sweeps away all the food.

rows.left: Both oppressing the poor to enrich oneself and giving to the rich yield only loss.
rows.full: Both oppressing the poor to enrich oneself and giving to the rich yield only loss.

rows.left: The wealth of the rich is his fortified city, like a high wall, in his own imagination.
rows.full: The wealth of the rich is his fortified city, like a high wall, in his own imagination.

rows.left: What the righteous hope for will end in joy
rows.right: what the wicked expect will come to nothing.
rows.full: What the righteous hope for will end in joy; what the wicked expect will come to nothing.

rows.left: The way of Adonai is a stronghold to the upright but ruin to those who do evil.
rows.full: The way of Adonai is a stronghold to the upright but ruin to those who do evil.

rows.left: The righteous will never be moved
rows.right: the wicked will not remain in the land.
rows.full: The righteous will never be moved, but the wicked will not remain in the land.

rows.left: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone or encroach on the land of the fatherless;
rows.full: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone or encroach on the land of the fatherless;

rows.left: for their Redeemer is strong; he will take up their fight against you.
rows.full: for their Redeemer is strong; he will take up their fight against you.

rows.left: No good comes from ill-gotten wealth
rows.right: righteousness rescues from death.
rows.full: No good comes from ill-gotten wealth, but righteousness rescues from death.

rows.left: The righteousness of the innocent levels their way
rows.right: wickedness of the wicked makes them fall.
rows.full: The righteousness of the innocent levels their way, but wickedness of the wicked makes them fall.

rows.left: When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes; what he hopes for from evil comes to nothing.
rows.full: When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes; what he hopes for from evil comes to nothing.

rows.left: Righteousness protects him whose way is honest
rows.right: wickedness brings down the sinner.
rows.full: Righteousness protects him whose way is honest, but wickedness brings down the sinner.

rows.left: The eyes of Adonai are everywhere, watching the evil and the good.
rows.full: The eyes of Adonai are everywhere, watching the evil and the good.

rows.left: Adonai detests the way of the wicked
rows.right: loves anyone who pursues righteousness.
rows.full: Adonai detests the way of the wicked but loves anyone who pursues righteousness.

rows.left: When a man’s ways please Adonai, he makes even the man’s enemies be at peace with him.
rows.full: When a man’s ways please Adonai, he makes even the man’s enemies be at peace with him.

rows.left: Evil will not depart from the house of him who returns evil for good.
rows.full: Evil will not depart from the house of him who returns evil for good.

rows.left: The words of a man’s mouth are deep water, a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.
rows.full: The words of a man’s mouth are deep water, a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.

rows.left: He who is kind to the poor is lending to Adonai; and he will repay him for his good deed.
rows.full: He who is kind to the poor is lending to Adonai; and he will repay him for his good deed.

rows.left: He who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, prosperity and honor.
rows.full: He who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, prosperity and honor.

rows.left: The clever see trouble coming and hide; the simple go on and pay the penalty.
rows.full: The clever see trouble coming and hide; the simple go on and pay the penalty.

rows.left: To a fool, vileness is like a game, as is wisdom to a person of discernment.
rows.full: To a fool, vileness is like a game, as is wisdom to a person of discernment.

rows.left: What a fool dreads will overtake him, but the righteous will be given his desire.
rows.full: What a fool dreads will overtake him, but the righteous will be given his desire.

rows.left: When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone
rows.right: but the righteous are firmly established forever.
rows.full: When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone; but the righteous are firmly established forever.

rows.left: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the duplicity of the treacherous destroys them.
rows.full: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the duplicity of the treacherous destroys them.

rows.left: A man who is kind does himself good, but the cruel does harm to himself.
rows.full: A man who is kind does himself good, but the cruel does harm to himself.

rows.left: The profits of the wicked are illusory
rows.right: but those who sow righteousness gain a true reward.
rows.full: The profits of the wicked are illusory; but those who sow righteousness gain a true reward.

rows.left: Genuine righteousness leads to life
rows.right: the pursuer of evil goes to his own death.
rows.full: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuer of evil goes to his own death.

rows.left: The crooked-hearted are an abomination to Adonai, but those sincere in their ways are his delight.
rows.full: The crooked-hearted are an abomination to Adonai, but those sincere in their ways are his delight.

rows.left: Depend on it: the evil will not go unpunished; but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
rows.full: Depend on it: the evil will not go unpunished; but the offspring of the righteous will escape.

rows.left: The righteous desire only good
rows.right: what the wicked hope for brings wrath.
rows.full: The righteous desire only good, but what the wicked hope for brings wrath.

rows.left: He who strives for good obtains favor, but he who searches for evil — it comes to him!
rows.full: He who strives for good obtains favor, but he who searches for evil — it comes to him!

rows.left: Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil, but for those advising peace there is joy.
rows.full: Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil, but for those advising peace there is joy.

rows.left: No harm can come to the righteous
rows.right: the wicked are overwhelmed with disaster.
rows.full: No harm can come to the righteous, but the wicked are overwhelmed with disaster.

rows.left: The light of the righteous [shines] joyfully
rows.right: the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
rows.full: The light of the righteous [shines] joyfully, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

rows.left: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will suffer.
rows.full: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will suffer.

rows.left: The fields of the poor may yield much food, but some are swept away because of injustice.
rows.full: The fields of the poor may yield much food, but some are swept away because of injustice.
