rows.left: No wisdom, discernment or counsel succeeds against Adonai.
rows.full: No wisdom, discernment or counsel succeeds against Adonai.

rows.right: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.
rows.full: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.

rows.right: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;
rows.full: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;

rows.left: He who remains stiffnecked after much rebuke will be suddenly and incurably broken.
rows.full: He who remains stiffnecked after much rebuke will be suddenly and incurably broken.

rows.left: The mind of a person with discernment gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
rows.full: The mind of a person with discernment gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

rows.left: Adonai, your eyes look for truth. You struck them
rows.right: they weren’t affected; you [nearly] destroyed them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock, refusing to repent.
rows.full: Adonai, your eyes look for truth. You struck them, but they weren’t affected; you [nearly] destroyed them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock, refusing to repent.

rows.left: A rebuke makes more impression on a person of understanding than a hundred blows on a fool.
rows.full: A rebuke makes more impression on a person of understanding than a hundred blows on a fool.

rows.left: Thoughtless people inherit folly, but the cautious are crowned with knowledge.
rows.full: Thoughtless people inherit folly, but the cautious are crowned with knowledge.

rows.left: Pay attention, and listen to the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge;
rows.full: Pay attention, and listen to the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge;

rows.left: My son, if you stop heeding discipline, you will stray from the principles of knowledge.
rows.full: My son, if you stop heeding discipline, you will stray from the principles of knowledge.

rows.left: A fool despises his father’s discipline
rows.right: he who heeds warnings is prudent.
rows.full: A fool despises his father’s discipline, but he who heeds warnings is prudent.

rows.left: The mind of a person with discernment seeks knowledge
rows.right: the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
rows.full: The mind of a person with discernment seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.

rows.left: A wise man is strong; yes, a man of knowledge grows in strength.
rows.full: A wise man is strong; yes, a man of knowledge grows in strength.

rows.right: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.
rows.full: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.

rows.right: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.
rows.full: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.

rows.left: Discipline your child while there is hope, but don’t get so angry that you kill him!
rows.full: Discipline your child while there is hope, but don’t get so angry that you kill him!

rows.right: “Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.
rows.full: “Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.

rows.right: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.
rows.full: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.

rows.left: Don’t withhold discipline from a child — if you beat him with a stick, he won’t die!
rows.full: Don’t withhold discipline from a child — if you beat him with a stick, he won’t die!

rows.right: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.right: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.
rows.full: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.

rows.right: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!
rows.full: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!

rows.right: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.
rows.full: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.

rows.left: He who trusts in himself is a fool
rows.right: he who lives by wisdom will escape.
rows.full: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but he who lives by wisdom will escape.

rows.left: The eyes of Adonai protect [the man with] knowledge, but he overturns the plans of a traitor.
rows.full: The eyes of Adonai protect [the man with] knowledge, but he overturns the plans of a traitor.

rows.left: Every cautious person acts with knowledge
rows.right: a fool parades his folly.
rows.full: Every cautious person acts with knowledge, but a fool parades his folly.

rows.right: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
rows.full: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

rows.right: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.
rows.full: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.

rows.right: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.left: If you strike a scorner, the simple will learn to act wisely; if you reprove the intelligent, he will understand what you mean.
rows.full: If you strike a scorner, the simple will learn to act wisely; if you reprove the intelligent, he will understand what you mean.

rows.left: For the mitzvah is a lamp, Torah is light, and reproofs that discipline are the way to life.
rows.full: For the mitzvah is a lamp, Torah is light, and reproofs that discipline are the way to life.

rows.right: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.
rows.full: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.

rows.right: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.
rows.full: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.

rows.right: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.
rows.full: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.

rows.right: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.
rows.full: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.

rows.left: He who fails to use a stick hates his son
rows.right: he who loves him is careful to discipline him.
rows.full: He who fails to use a stick hates his son, but he who loves him is careful to discipline him.

rows.right: The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.
rows.full: The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.

rows.left: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a patron of prostitutes wastes his wealth.
rows.full: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a patron of prostitutes wastes his wealth.

rows.left: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will be your delight.
rows.full: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will be your delight.

rows.left: The discerning person focuses on wisdom there before him
rows.right: a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
rows.full: The discerning person focuses on wisdom there before him, but a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.

rows.right: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;
rows.full: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;

rows.left: Buy the truth, don’t sell it, also wisdom, discipline and discernment.
rows.full: Buy the truth, don’t sell it, also wisdom, discipline and discernment.

rows.left: Doing wrong is firmly tied to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away from him.
rows.full: Doing wrong is firmly tied to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away from him.

rows.right: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.
rows.full: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.

rows.left: When a scorner is punished, the simple become wiser; and when the wise is instructed, he takes hold of knowledge.
rows.full: When a scorner is punished, the simple become wiser; and when the wise is instructed, he takes hold of knowledge.

rows.right: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.
rows.full: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.

rows.left: A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls, but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.
rows.full: A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls, but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.

rows.left: Apply your mind to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.
rows.full: Apply your mind to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.

rows.left: A wise-hearted person is said to have discernment, and sweetness of speech adds to learning.
rows.full: A wise-hearted person is said to have discernment, and sweetness of speech adds to learning.

rows.left: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
rows.full: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.

rows.right: It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city; their fights are like the bars of a fortress.
rows.full: It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city; their fights are like the bars of a fortress.

rows.left: For with clever strategy you wage your war, and victory comes from having many advisers.
rows.full: For with clever strategy you wage your war, and victory comes from having many advisers.

rows.left: Yah disciplined me severely, but did not hand me over to death.
rows.full: Yah disciplined me severely, but did not hand me over to death.

rows.left: He who despises a word will suffer for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.
rows.full: He who despises a word will suffer for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.

rows.left: If you entrust all you do to Adonai, your plans will achieve success.
rows.full: If you entrust all you do to Adonai, your plans will achieve success.

rows.left: for it is pleasant to keep them deep within you; have all of them ready on your lips.
rows.full: for it is pleasant to keep them deep within you; have all of them ready on your lips.

rows.left: I want your trust to be in Adonai; this is why I’m instructing you about them today.
rows.full: I want your trust to be in Adonai; this is why I’m instructing you about them today.

rows.left: so you will know that these sayings are certainly true and bring back true sayings to him who sent you.
rows.full: so you will know that these sayings are certainly true and bring back true sayings to him who sent you.

rows.left: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
rows.full: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.

rows.left: Without clever tactics an army is defeated, and victory comes from much planning.
rows.full: Without clever tactics an army is defeated, and victory comes from much planning.

rows.right: A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense, but a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.
rows.full: A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense, but a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.

rows.left: Fools suppose their way is straight, but the wise pay attention to advice.
rows.full: Fools suppose their way is straight, but the wise pay attention to advice.

rows.left: Poverty and shame are for him who won’t be taught, but he who heeds reproof will be honored.
rows.full: Poverty and shame are for him who won’t be taught, but he who heeds reproof will be honored.

rows.right: A person with upright conduct fears Adonai, but a person who is devious scorns him.
rows.full: A person with upright conduct fears Adonai, but a person who is devious scorns him.

rows.left: The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going
rows.right: the folly of fools misleads them.
rows.full: The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going, but the folly of fools misleads them.

rows.right: Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools; but among the upright there is good will.
rows.full: Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools; but among the upright there is good will.

rows.left: A scorner does not like being corrected; he won’t go to the wise [for advice].
rows.full: A scorner does not like being corrected; he won’t go to the wise [for advice].

rows.left: A wise son is a joy to his father, and only a fool despises his mother.
rows.full: A wise son is a joy to his father, and only a fool despises his mother.

rows.left: Without deliberation, plans go wrong; but with many advisers, they succeed.
rows.full: Without deliberation, plans go wrong; but with many advisers, they succeed.

rows.right: All a man’s ways are pure in his own view, but Adonai weighs the spirit.
rows.full: All a man’s ways are pure in his own view, but Adonai weighs the spirit.

rows.right: Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.
rows.full: Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.

rows.right: One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.
rows.full: One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.

rows.left: He who controls his temper is better than a war hero, he who rules his spirit better than he who captures a city.
rows.full: He who controls his temper is better than a war hero, he who rules his spirit better than he who captures a city.

rows.right: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but the one who tests hearts is Adonai.
rows.full: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but the one who tests hearts is Adonai.

rows.right: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.
rows.full: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.

rows.left: He who fathers a fool does so to his sorrow, and the father of a boor has no joy.
rows.full: He who fathers a fool does so to his sorrow, and the father of a boor has no joy.

rows.left: A son who is a fool means anger for his father and bitterness for the mother who gave him birth.
rows.full: A son who is a fool means anger for his father and bitterness for the mother who gave him birth.

rows.right: He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.
rows.full: He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.

rows.left: To acquire good sense is to love oneself; to treasure discernment is to prosper.
rows.full: To acquire good sense is to love oneself; to treasure discernment is to prosper.

rows.left: After consultation, plans succeed; so take wise advice when waging war.
rows.full: After consultation, plans succeed; so take wise advice when waging war.

rows.left: Blows that wound purge away evil, yes, beatings [cleanse] one’s inmost being.
rows.full: Blows that wound purge away evil, yes, beatings [cleanse] one’s inmost being.

rows.right: All a person’s ways are right in his own view, but Adonai weighs the heart.
rows.full: All a person’s ways are right in his own view, but Adonai weighs the heart.

rows.right: The wicked is set on evil; he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.
rows.full: The wicked is set on evil; he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.

rows.right: The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.
rows.full: The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.

rows.right: Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.
rows.full: Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.

rows.right: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.
rows.full: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.

rows.left: If you beat him with a stick, you will save him from Sh’ol.
rows.full: If you beat him with a stick, you will save him from Sh’ol.

rows.left: My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart too is glad;
rows.full: My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart too is glad;

rows.left: my inmost being rejoices when your lips say what is right.
rows.full: my inmost being rejoices when your lips say what is right.

rows.right: for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.
rows.full: for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.

rows.right: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.
rows.full: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.

rows.right: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.
rows.full: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.

rows.left: My son, eat honey, for it is good; honeycomb drippings are sweet to your taste.
rows.full: My son, eat honey, for it is good; honeycomb drippings are sweet to your taste.

rows.right: Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.
rows.full: Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.

rows.left: Like a city breached, without walls, is a person who lacks self-control.
rows.full: Like a city breached, without walls, is a person who lacks self-control.

rows.right: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.
rows.full: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.

rows.left: My son, become wise, and gladden my heart, so that I can answer my critics.
rows.full: My son, become wise, and gladden my heart, so that I can answer my critics.

rows.right: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.
rows.full: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.

rows.left: The rich man is wise in his own view, but the poor who has discernment sees through him.
rows.full: The rich man is wise in his own view, but the poor who has discernment sees through him.

rows.right: Happy the person who is never without fear, but he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.
rows.full: Happy the person who is never without fear, but he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.

rows.right: Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.
rows.full: Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.

rows.left: Without a prophetic vision, the people throw off all restraint; but he who keeps Torah is happy.
rows.full: Without a prophetic vision, the people throw off all restraint; but he who keeps Torah is happy.

rows.left: A slave can’t be disciplined with words; he may understand, but he won’t respond.
rows.full: A slave can’t be disciplined with words; he may understand, but he won’t respond.

rows.left: A slave who is pampered from youth will in the end be ungrateful.
rows.full: A slave who is pampered from youth will in the end be ungrateful.

rows.right: The proud will be humbled, but the humble will be honored.
rows.full: The proud will be humbled, but the humble will be honored.

rows.left: The fear of Adonai is the beginning of knowledge
rows.right: fools despise wisdom and discipline.
rows.full: The fear of Adonai is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.

rows.right: A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
rows.full: A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

rows.right: The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.
rows.full: The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.

rows.right: For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.
rows.full: For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.

rows.left: “How happy the person whom God corrects! So don’t despise Shaddai’s discipline.
rows.full: “How happy the person whom God corrects! So don’t despise Shaddai’s discipline.

rows.left: The discipline of wisdom is fear of Adonai, so before being honored, a person must be humble.
rows.full: The discipline of wisdom is fear of Adonai, so before being honored, a person must be humble.

rows.left: Also you have forgotten the counsel which speaks with you as sons: “My son, don’t despise the discipline of Adonai or become despondent when he corrects you. For Adonai disciplines those he loves and whips everyone he accepts as a son.”
rows.full: Also you have forgotten the counsel which speaks with you as sons: “My son, don’t despise the discipline of Adonai or become despondent when he corrects you. For Adonai disciplines those he loves and whips everyone he accepts as a son.”

rows.left: As for me, I rebuke and discipline everyone I love; so exert yourselves, and turn from your sins!
rows.full: As for me, I rebuke and discipline everyone I love; so exert yourselves, and turn from your sins!

rows.right: First comes pride, then disgrace; but with the humble is wisdom.
rows.full: First comes pride, then disgrace; but with the humble is wisdom.

rows.right: Better to be humble among the poor than share the spoil with the proud.
rows.full: Better to be humble among the poor than share the spoil with the proud.

rows.right: Before being ruined, a person’s heart is proud; before being honored, a person must be humble.
rows.full: Before being ruined, a person’s heart is proud; before being honored, a person must be humble.

rows.left: For they disciplined us only for a short time and only as best they could; but he disciplines us in a way that provides genuine benefit to us and enables us to share in his holiness. Now, all discipline, while it is happening, does indeed seem painful, not enjoyable; but for those who have been trained by it, it later produces its peaceful fruit, which is righteousness.
rows.full: For they disciplined us only for a short time and only as best they could; but he disciplines us in a way that provides genuine benefit to us and enables us to share in his holiness. Now, all discipline, while it is happening, does indeed seem painful, not enjoyable; but for those who have been trained by it, it later produces its peaceful fruit, which is righteousness.

rows.right: Haughty looks, a proud heart — what the wicked plow is sin.
rows.full: Haughty looks, a proud heart — what the wicked plow is sin.

rows.left: A scoffer seeks wisdom in vain
rows.right: knowledge comes easily to someone with discernment.
rows.full: A scoffer seeks wisdom in vain, but knowledge comes easily to someone with discernment.

rows.left: Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.
rows.full: Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.

rows.left: In the fear of Adonai is powerful security; for his children there will be a place of refuge.
rows.full: In the fear of Adonai is powerful security; for his children there will be a place of refuge.

rows.left: He who spurns discipline detests himself, but he who listens to correction grows in understanding.
rows.full: He who spurns discipline detests himself, but he who listens to correction grows in understanding.

rows.right: Adonai will pull down the houses of the proud, but preserves intact the widow’s boundaries.
rows.full: Adonai will pull down the houses of the proud, but preserves intact the widow’s boundaries.

rows.right: Adonai detests all those with proud hearts; be assured that they will not go unpunished.
rows.full: Adonai detests all those with proud hearts; be assured that they will not go unpunished.

rows.right: Pride goes before destruction, and arrogance before failure.
rows.full: Pride goes before destruction, and arrogance before failure.

rows.right: Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.
rows.full: Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.

rows.right: When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.
rows.full: When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.

rows.right: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.
rows.full: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.

rows.right: Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.
rows.full: Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.

rows.right: Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.
rows.full: Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.

rows.right: Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.
rows.full: Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.

rows.right: A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.
rows.full: A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.

rows.right: You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.
rows.full: You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.

rows.left: The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame on his mother.
rows.full: The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame on his mother.

rows.left: A son who heeds his father’s discipline is wise
rows.right: a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
rows.full: A son who heeds his father’s discipline is wise, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.

rows.left: Listen to advice, and accept discipline, so that in the end you will be wise.
rows.full: Listen to advice, and accept discipline, so that in the end you will be wise.

rows.left: He who loves knowledge loves discipline
rows.right: he who hates correction is a boor.
rows.full: He who loves knowledge loves discipline, but he who hates correction is a boor.

rows.left: Therefore, say to them, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of Adonai their God. They won’t take correction; faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their mouths.
rows.full: Therefore, say to them, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of Adonai their God. They won’t take correction; faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their mouths.

rows.right: A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.
rows.full: A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.

rows.left: The fear of Adonai is a fountain of life enabling one to avoid deadly traps.
rows.full: The fear of Adonai is a fountain of life enabling one to avoid deadly traps.

rows.left: How much better than gold it is to gain wisdom! Yes, rather than money, choose to gain understanding.
rows.full: How much better than gold it is to gain wisdom! Yes, rather than money, choose to gain understanding.

rows.left: How happy the man whom you correct, Yah, whom you teach from your Torah,
rows.full: How happy the man whom you correct, Yah, whom you teach from your Torah,

rows.left: Know that wisdom is similar[ly sweet] to your soul; if you find it, then you will have a future, what you hope for will not be cut off.
rows.full: Know that wisdom is similar[ly sweet] to your soul; if you find it, then you will have a future, what you hope for will not be cut off.

rows.right: He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.
rows.full: He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.

rows.right: Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what the day may bring.
rows.full: Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what the day may bring.

rows.left: He who heeds life-giving correction will be at home in the company of the wise.
rows.full: He who heeds life-giving correction will be at home in the company of the wise.

rows.left: I have written you worthwhile things full of good counsel and knowledge,
rows.full: I have written you worthwhile things full of good counsel and knowledge,

rows.left: Why would a fool wish to pay for wisdom when he has no desire to learn?
rows.full: Why would a fool wish to pay for wisdom when he has no desire to learn?

rows.left: Insolence produces only strife, but wisdom is found with those who take advice.
rows.full: Insolence produces only strife, but wisdom is found with those who take advice.

rows.left: Wisdom is at rest in a person with discernment
rows.right: in fools it has to call attention to itself.
rows.full: Wisdom is at rest in a person with discernment, but in fools it has to call attention to itself.

rows.left: No wisdom, discernment or counsel succeeds against Adonai.
rows.full: No wisdom, discernment or counsel succeeds against Adonai.

rows.right: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.
rows.full: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.

rows.right: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;
rows.full: Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;

rows.left: He who remains stiffnecked after much rebuke will be suddenly and incurably broken.
rows.full: He who remains stiffnecked after much rebuke will be suddenly and incurably broken.

rows.left: The mind of a person with discernment gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
rows.full: The mind of a person with discernment gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

rows.left: Adonai, your eyes look for truth. You struck them
rows.right: they weren’t affected; you [nearly] destroyed them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock, refusing to repent.
rows.full: Adonai, your eyes look for truth. You struck them, but they weren’t affected; you [nearly] destroyed them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock, refusing to repent.

rows.left: A rebuke makes more impression on a person of understanding than a hundred blows on a fool.
rows.full: A rebuke makes more impression on a person of understanding than a hundred blows on a fool.

rows.left: Thoughtless people inherit folly, but the cautious are crowned with knowledge.
rows.full: Thoughtless people inherit folly, but the cautious are crowned with knowledge.

rows.left: Pay attention, and listen to the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge;
rows.full: Pay attention, and listen to the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge;

rows.left: My son, if you stop heeding discipline, you will stray from the principles of knowledge.
rows.full: My son, if you stop heeding discipline, you will stray from the principles of knowledge.

rows.left: A fool despises his father’s discipline
rows.right: he who heeds warnings is prudent.
rows.full: A fool despises his father’s discipline, but he who heeds warnings is prudent.

rows.left: The mind of a person with discernment seeks knowledge
rows.right: the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
rows.full: The mind of a person with discernment seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.

rows.left: A wise man is strong; yes, a man of knowledge grows in strength.
rows.full: A wise man is strong; yes, a man of knowledge grows in strength.

rows.right: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.
rows.full: Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.

rows.right: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.
rows.full: Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.

rows.left: Discipline your child while there is hope, but don’t get so angry that you kill him!
rows.full: Discipline your child while there is hope, but don’t get so angry that you kill him!

rows.right: “Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.
rows.full: “Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.

rows.right: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.
rows.full: A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.

rows.left: Don’t withhold discipline from a child — if you beat him with a stick, he won’t die!
rows.full: Don’t withhold discipline from a child — if you beat him with a stick, he won’t die!

rows.right: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.right: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.
rows.full: Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.

rows.right: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!
rows.full: Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!

rows.right: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.
rows.full: Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.

rows.left: He who trusts in himself is a fool
rows.right: he who lives by wisdom will escape.
rows.full: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but he who lives by wisdom will escape.

rows.left: The eyes of Adonai protect [the man with] knowledge, but he overturns the plans of a traitor.
rows.full: The eyes of Adonai protect [the man with] knowledge, but he overturns the plans of a traitor.

rows.left: Every cautious person acts with knowledge
rows.right: a fool parades his folly.
rows.full: Every cautious person acts with knowledge, but a fool parades his folly.

rows.right: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
rows.full: An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

rows.right: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.
rows.full: It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.

rows.right: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
rows.full: Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

rows.left: If you strike a scorner, the simple will learn to act wisely; if you reprove the intelligent, he will understand what you mean.
rows.full: If you strike a scorner, the simple will learn to act wisely; if you reprove the intelligent, he will understand what you mean.

rows.left: For the mitzvah is a lamp, Torah is light, and reproofs that discipline are the way to life.
rows.full: For the mitzvah is a lamp, Torah is light, and reproofs that discipline are the way to life.

rows.right: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.
rows.full: Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.

rows.right: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.
rows.full: The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.

rows.right: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.
rows.full: but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.

rows.right: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.
rows.full: When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.

rows.left: He who fails to use a stick hates his son
rows.right: he who loves him is careful to discipline him.
rows.full: He who fails to use a stick hates his son, but he who loves him is careful to discipline him.

rows.right: The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.
rows.full: The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.

rows.left: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a patron of prostitutes wastes his wealth.
rows.full: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a patron of prostitutes wastes his wealth.

rows.left: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will be your delight.
rows.full: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will be your delight.

rows.left: The discerning person focuses on wisdom there before him
rows.right: a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
rows.full: The discerning person focuses on wisdom there before him, but a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.

rows.right: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;
rows.full: Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;

rows.left: Buy the truth, don’t sell it, also wisdom, discipline and discernment.
rows.full: Buy the truth, don’t sell it, also wisdom, discipline and discernment.

rows.left: Doing wrong is firmly tied to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away from him.
rows.full: Doing wrong is firmly tied to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away from him.

rows.right: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.
rows.full: The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.

rows.left: When a scorner is punished, the simple become wiser; and when the wise is instructed, he takes hold of knowledge.
rows.full: When a scorner is punished, the simple become wiser; and when the wise is instructed, he takes hold of knowledge.

rows.right: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.
rows.full: Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.

rows.left: A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls, but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.
rows.full: A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls, but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.

rows.left: Apply your mind to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.
rows.full: Apply your mind to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.

rows.left: A wise-hearted person is said to have discernment, and sweetness of speech adds to learning.
rows.full: A wise-hearted person is said to have discernment, and sweetness of speech adds to learning.

rows.left: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
rows.full: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.

rows.right: It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city; their fights are like the bars of a fortress.
rows.full: It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city; their fights are like the bars of a fortress.

rows.left: For with clever strategy you wage your war, and victory comes from having many advisers.
rows.full: For with clever strategy you wage your war, and victory comes from having many advisers.

rows.left: Yah disciplined me severely, but did not hand me over to death.
rows.full: Yah disciplined me severely, but did not hand me over to death.

rows.left: He who despises a word will suffer for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.
rows.full: He who despises a word will suffer for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.

rows.left: If you entrust all you do to Adonai, your plans will achieve success.
rows.full: If you entrust all you do to Adonai, your plans will achieve success.

rows.left: for it is pleasant to keep them deep within you; have all of them ready on your lips.
rows.full: for it is pleasant to keep them deep within you; have all of them ready on your lips.

rows.left: I want your trust to be in Adonai; this is why I’m instructing you about them today.
rows.full: I want your trust to be in Adonai; this is why I’m instructing you about them today.

rows.left: so you will know that these sayings are certainly true and bring back true sayings to him who sent you.
rows.full: so you will know that these sayings are certainly true and bring back true sayings to him who sent you.

rows.left: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
rows.full: The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.

rows.left: Without clever tactics an army is defeated, and victory comes from much planning.
rows.full: Without clever tactics an army is defeated, and victory comes from much planning.

rows.right: A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense, but a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.
rows.full: A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense, but a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.

rows.left: Fools suppose their way is straight, but the wise pay attention to advice.
rows.full: Fools suppose their way is straight, but the wise pay attention to advice.

rows.left: Poverty and shame are for him who won’t be taught, but he who heeds reproof will be honored.
rows.full: Poverty and shame are for him who won’t be taught, but he who heeds reproof will be honored.

rows.right: A person with upright conduct fears Adonai, but a person who is devious scorns him.
rows.full: A person with upright conduct fears Adonai, but a person who is devious scorns him.

rows.left: The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going
rows.right: the folly of fools misleads them.
rows.full: The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going, but the folly of fools misleads them.

rows.right: Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools; but among the upright there is good will.
rows.full: Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools; but among the upright there is good will.

rows.left: A scorner does not like being corrected; he won’t go to the wise [for advice].
rows.full: A scorner does not like being corrected; he won’t go to the wise [for advice].

rows.left: A wise son is a joy to his father, and only a fool despises his mother.
rows.full: A wise son is a joy to his father, and only a fool despises his mother.

rows.left: Without deliberation, plans go wrong; but with many advisers, they succeed.
rows.full: Without deliberation, plans go wrong; but with many advisers, they succeed.

rows.right: All a man’s ways are pure in his own view, but Adonai weighs the spirit.
rows.full: All a man’s ways are pure in his own view, but Adonai weighs the spirit.

rows.right: Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.
rows.full: Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.

rows.right: One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.
rows.full: One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.

rows.left: He who controls his temper is better than a war hero, he who rules his spirit better than he who captures a city.
rows.full: He who controls his temper is better than a war hero, he who rules his spirit better than he who captures a city.

rows.right: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but the one who tests hearts is Adonai.
rows.full: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but the one who tests hearts is Adonai.

rows.right: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.
rows.full: Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.

rows.left: He who fathers a fool does so to his sorrow, and the father of a boor has no joy.
rows.full: He who fathers a fool does so to his sorrow, and the father of a boor has no joy.

rows.left: A son who is a fool means anger for his father and bitterness for the mother who gave him birth.
rows.full: A son who is a fool means anger for his father and bitterness for the mother who gave him birth.

rows.right: He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.
rows.full: He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.

rows.left: To acquire good sense is to love oneself; to treasure discernment is to prosper.
rows.full: To acquire good sense is to love oneself; to treasure discernment is to prosper.

rows.left: After consultation, plans succeed; so take wise advice when waging war.
rows.full: After consultation, plans succeed; so take wise advice when waging war.

rows.left: Blows that wound purge away evil, yes, beatings [cleanse] one’s inmost being.
rows.full: Blows that wound purge away evil, yes, beatings [cleanse] one’s inmost being.

rows.right: All a person’s ways are right in his own view, but Adonai weighs the heart.
rows.full: All a person’s ways are right in his own view, but Adonai weighs the heart.

rows.right: The wicked is set on evil; he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.
rows.full: The wicked is set on evil; he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.

rows.right: The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.
rows.full: The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.

rows.right: Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.
rows.full: Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.

rows.right: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.
rows.full: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.

rows.left: If you beat him with a stick, you will save him from Sh’ol.
rows.full: If you beat him with a stick, you will save him from Sh’ol.

rows.left: My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart too is glad;
rows.full: My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart too is glad;

rows.left: my inmost being rejoices when your lips say what is right.
rows.full: my inmost being rejoices when your lips say what is right.

rows.right: for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.
rows.full: for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.

rows.right: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.
rows.full: Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.

rows.right: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.
rows.full: For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.

rows.left: My son, eat honey, for it is good; honeycomb drippings are sweet to your taste.
rows.full: My son, eat honey, for it is good; honeycomb drippings are sweet to your taste.

rows.right: Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.
rows.full: Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.

rows.left: Like a city breached, without walls, is a person who lacks self-control.
rows.full: Like a city breached, without walls, is a person who lacks self-control.

rows.right: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.
rows.full: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.

rows.left: My son, become wise, and gladden my heart, so that I can answer my critics.
rows.full: My son, become wise, and gladden my heart, so that I can answer my critics.

rows.right: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.
rows.full: The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.

rows.left: The rich man is wise in his own view, but the poor who has discernment sees through him.
rows.full: The rich man is wise in his own view, but the poor who has discernment sees through him.

rows.right: Happy the person who is never without fear, but he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.
rows.full: Happy the person who is never without fear, but he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.

rows.right: Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.
rows.full: Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.

rows.left: Without a prophetic vision, the people throw off all restraint; but he who keeps Torah is happy.
rows.full: Without a prophetic vision, the people throw off all restraint; but he who keeps Torah is happy.

rows.left: A slave can’t be disciplined with words; he may understand, but he won’t respond.
rows.full: A slave can’t be disciplined with words; he may understand, but he won’t respond.

rows.left: A slave who is pampered from youth will in the end be ungrateful.
rows.full: A slave who is pampered from youth will in the end be ungrateful.

rows.right: The human spirit is a lamp of Adonai; it searches one’s inmost being.
rows.full: The human spirit is a lamp of Adonai; it searches one’s inmost being.

rows.left: “How happy the person whom God corrects! So don’t despise Shaddai’s discipline.
rows.full: “How happy the person whom God corrects! So don’t despise Shaddai’s discipline.

rows.left: Also you have forgotten the counsel which speaks with you as sons: “My son, don’t despise the discipline of Adonai or become despondent when he corrects you. For Adonai disciplines those he loves and whips everyone he accepts as a son.”
rows.full: Also you have forgotten the counsel which speaks with you as sons: “My son, don’t despise the discipline of Adonai or become despondent when he corrects you. For Adonai disciplines those he loves and whips everyone he accepts as a son.”

rows.left: As for me, I rebuke and discipline everyone I love; so exert yourselves, and turn from your sins!
rows.full: As for me, I rebuke and discipline everyone I love; so exert yourselves, and turn from your sins!

rows.right: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
rows.full: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.

rows.left: For they disciplined us only for a short time and only as best they could; but he disciplines us in a way that provides genuine benefit to us and enables us to share in his holiness. Now, all discipline, while it is happening, does indeed seem painful, not enjoyable; but for those who have been trained by it, it later produces its peaceful fruit, which is righteousness.
rows.full: For they disciplined us only for a short time and only as best they could; but he disciplines us in a way that provides genuine benefit to us and enables us to share in his holiness. Now, all discipline, while it is happening, does indeed seem painful, not enjoyable; but for those who have been trained by it, it later produces its peaceful fruit, which is righteousness.

rows.left: Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.
rows.full: Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.

rows.left: He who spurns discipline detests himself, but he who listens to correction grows in understanding.
rows.full: He who spurns discipline detests himself, but he who listens to correction grows in understanding.

rows.right: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share its joy.
rows.full: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share its joy.

rows.right: Even in laughter the heart can be sad, and joy may end in sorrow.
rows.full: Even in laughter the heart can be sad, and joy may end in sorrow.

rows.right: A glad heart makes a face happy, but heartache breaks the spirit.
rows.full: A glad heart makes a face happy, but heartache breaks the spirit.

rows.right: A cheerful glance brings joy to the heart, and good news invigorates the bones.
rows.full: A cheerful glance brings joy to the heart, and good news invigorates the bones.

rows.right: A happy heart is good medicine, but low spirits sap one’s strength.
rows.full: A happy heart is good medicine, but low spirits sap one’s strength.

rows.right: Like removing clothes on a chilly day or like vinegar on soda is someone who sings songs to a heavy heart.
rows.full: Like removing clothes on a chilly day or like vinegar on soda is someone who sings songs to a heavy heart.

rows.left: The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame on his mother.
rows.full: The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame on his mother.

rows.left: A son who heeds his father’s discipline is wise, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
rows.full: A son who heeds his father’s discipline is wise, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.

rows.left: Listen to advice, and accept discipline, so that in the end you will be wise.
rows.full: Listen to advice, and accept discipline, so that in the end you will be wise.

rows.left: He who loves knowledge loves discipline, but he who hates correction is a boor.
rows.full: He who loves knowledge loves discipline, but he who hates correction is a boor.

rows.left: Therefore, say to them, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of Adonai their God. They won’t take correction; faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their mouths.
rows.full: Therefore, say to them, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of Adonai their God. They won’t take correction; faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their mouths.

rows.right: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning away from evil is abhorrent to fools.
rows.full: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning away from evil is abhorrent to fools.

rows.left: How happy the man whom you correct, Yah, whom you teach from your Torah,
rows.full: How happy the man whom you correct, Yah, whom you teach from your Torah,

rows.right: The hearing ear and the seeing eye — Adonai made them both.
rows.full: The hearing ear and the seeing eye — Adonai made them both.

rows.right: If you have a big appetite, put a knife to your throat!
rows.full: If you have a big appetite, put a knife to your throat!

rows.full: Who has misery? Who has regret? Who fights and complains all the time? Who gets bruised for no good reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?

rows.full: Your eyes will see peculiar things, your mind will utter nonsense.

rows.left: He who heeds life-giving correction will be at home in the company of the wise.

rows.left: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.

rows.right: Wine is a mocker, strong liquor a rowdy; anyone led astray by it is unwise.
